I’m 33, not old, but I’ve farmed these 5 years long enough to know I can’t bet the whole 163 mu on one idea. Wheat-maize is still my backbone, so I keep 90 mu in that double crop because it is the steadiest and I know the field rhythm well. The rest I spread into cotton, stevia, watermelon, broccoli, and chili. That way if grain price is weak, I still have some cash crops; if vegetables get hit by disease or price falls, I still have wheat and maize. My schooling is middle level, so I do listen to the extension guy about split fertilizer and timing, but I still farm mostly by what worked on my own land and what I see nearby.

Because some people in my family work off-farm, I can’t make the whole farm too labor-heavy. Broccoli and chili make money, but they tie up people and need more spraying and watering, so I keep them limited. Cotton and stevia I can still manage with hired help at peak time. On wheat I will not save too much on fertilizer because missing yield there hurts the whole year. On maize I plant fast right after wheat harvest, with simple tillage, otherwise I lose moisture and the season gets late. With well irrigation I can secure key stages, but pumping costs money, so I won’t water just because the calendar says so. I’ll water when wheat jointing and grain fill need it, and for maize and cash crops when the soil is really short of moisture. Overall I want a steady year, not a fancy year.
